completed.name: DLMF.AlgebraicAnalytic.sum_rpow_le_of_forall_inner_le
completed.doc:
DLMF §1.7(i), converse of Hölder's inequality: for `p > 1`, `1/p + 1/q = 1`, `aⱼ ≥ 0` and
`A, B > 0`, if `∑ aⱼbⱼ ≤ A^{1/p} B^{1/q}` for all `bⱼ ≥ 0` with `∑ bⱼ^q ≤ B`, then
`∑ aⱼᵖ ≤ A`.

completed.name: DLMF.AlgebraicAnalytic.min_le_powerMean_le_max
completed.doc:
DLMF 1.7.8: for `r ≠ 0`, positive `aⱼ` and weights `pⱼ > 0` with `∑ pⱼ = 1`, the
weighted mean `M(r) = (∑ pⱼ aⱼ^r)^{1/r}` lies between `min aⱼ` and `max aⱼ`, with equality
(on either side) iff `a₁ = ⋯ = aₙ`. (DLMF's further case `r < 0` with some `aⱼ = 0` is the
convention `M(r) = 0 = min aⱼ` of 1.2.22.)

completed.name: DLMF.AlgebraicAnalytic.powerMean_le_powerMean
completed.doc:
DLMF 1.7.9: for positive `aⱼ`, weights `pⱼ > 0` with `∑ pⱼ = 1`, and nonzero `r < s`,
`M(r) ≤ M(s)`, with equality iff all `aⱼ` are equal.

completed.name: DLMF.AlgebraicAnalytic.schwarz_lemma_eq_iff
completed.doc:
DLMF 1.10.11 (Schwarz's lemma, equality case): under the hypotheses of 1.10.11, equality
`|f(z₁)| = M|z₁|/R` at some `z₁ ≠ 0` or `|f'(0)| = M/R` holds iff `f(z) = Az` on `|z| < R`
with `|A| = M/R`.

completed.name: DLMF.AlgebraicAnalytic.coeff_eq_circleIntegral

DLMF 1.10.26–1.10.27: if `F(z) = ∑ pₙ zⁿ` for `|z| < R` (the generating function of the

newHelpers.name: DLMF.JacobiElliptic.jacobiSnk_dslope_regular
newHelpers.doc:
Dividing `sn(z,k)` by `z` with Mathlib's `dslope` removes the origin zero.
The quotient is analytic at every real argument, equals one at zero, and has zero
derivative there because `sn` is odd.

newHelpers.name: DLMF.JacobiElliptic.jacobiSnm_ne_zero_between

newHelpers.name: DLMF.JacobiElliptic.jacobiNs_regularized_primitive
newHelpers.doc:
The regularized expression `1/t+t-cn(t)dn(t)/sn(t)` extends to a smooth real
primitive vanishing at zero. Its derivative away from zero is
`ns(t)²-t⁻²+dn(t)²`; analyticity of the divided Jacobi sine supplies the extension.

newHelpers.name: DLMF.JacobiElliptic.jacobiEpsilonk_ns_integral_aux
newHelpers.doc:
The regularized `ns²` integrand is integrable across the origin. Its primitive
gives the epsilon integral formula, with the point value at zero handled by almost
everywhere equality.

newHelpers.name: DLMF.JacobiElliptic.jacobiNs_sq_integral_shift

A squared identity `v²+α sn²=1` changes the regularized `ns²` integral by `-αx`.
This applies to both `v=dn`, `α=k²` and `v=cn`, `α=1`.

newIssues.reproductionSource:
import DLMF.Theta.PowerSeries
import DLMF.JacobiElliptic.Basic.QuarterPeriods
open Complex Set
open scoped Real
namespace DLMF.Theta

lemma lattice_norm_ge (p : {p : ℤ × ℤ // p ≠ 0}) :
    1 ≤ ‖((p.1.1 : ℂ) + p.1.2 * I)‖ := by
  have hp : p.1.1 ≠ 0 ∨ p.1.2 ≠ 0 := by
    by_contra h
    push_neg at h
    exact p.2 (Prod.ext h.1 h.2)
  have hi : (1 : ℤ) ≤ p.1.1 ^ 2 + p.1.2 ^ 2 := by
    rcases hp with h | h
    · have h2 : p.1.1 ≤ -1 ∨ 1 ≤ p.1.1 := by omega
      rcases h2 with h2 | h2 <;> nlinarith [sq_nonneg p.1.2]
    · have h2 : p.1.2 ≤ -1 ∨ 1 ≤ p.1.2 := by omega
      rcases h2 with h2 | h2 <;> nlinarith [sq_nonneg p.1.1]
  have hr : (1 : ℝ) ≤ (p.1.1 : ℝ) ^ 2 + (p.1.2 : ℝ) ^ 2 := by exact_mod_cast hi
  have hn := Complex.sq_norm ((p.1.1 : ℂ) + p.1.2 * I)
  simp only [normSq_apply, add_re, add_im, intCast_re, intCast_im, mul_re, mul_im, I_re, I_im,
    mul_zero, zero_mul, mul_one, sub_zero, zero_add, add_zero] at hn
  nlinarith [norm_nonneg ((p.1.1 : ℂ) + p.1.2 * I)]

lemma radius_ge : Real.pi ≤ thetaLatticeMinNorm I := by
  letI : Nonempty {p : ℤ × ℤ // p ≠ 0} := ⟨⟨(1,0), by decide⟩⟩
  apply le_ciInf
  intro p
  rw [norm_mul, Complex.norm_real, Real.norm_of_nonneg Real.pi_pos.le]
  nlinarith [lattice_norm_ge p, Real.pi_pos]

lemma condition : ‖(π : ℂ) * (1 / 2 : ℂ)‖ < thetaLatticeMinNorm I := by
  calc ‖(π : ℂ) * (1 / 2 : ℂ)‖ = Real.pi / 2 := by simp [div_eq_mul_inv, Real.norm_of_nonneg Real.pi_pos.le]
    _ < Real.pi := by linarith [Real.pi_pos]
    _ ≤ _ := radius_ge

lemma theta_two_zero : DLMF.Elliptic.jacobiThetaTwoTau ((π : ℂ) * (1 / 2 : ℂ)) I = 0 := by
  have h := DLMF.JacobiElliptic.je22a_thetaTwo_add_half_pi 0 I
  have h0 := DLMF.Theta.jacobiThetaOneTau_lattice_eq_zero I 0 0
  simp only [Int.cast_zero, zero_mul, zero_add, mul_zero, neg_zero] at h0
  simpa [h0, div_eq_mul_inv] using h

lemma counterexample : ¬ (∃ S : ℂ,
    HasSum (fun j : ℕ => thetaAlpha (2 * (j + 1)) I * (1 / 2 : ℂ) ^ (2 * (j + 1)) /
      (2 * (j + 1))) S ∧
    DLMF.Elliptic.jacobiThetaTwoTau ((π : ℂ) * (1 / 2 : ℂ)) I =
      jacobiThetaTwoNullTau I * cexp (-S)) := by
  rintro ⟨S, _, h⟩
  rw [theta_two_zero] at h
  exact (mul_ne_zero (DLMF.JacobiElliptic.je22a_thetaTwo_zero_ne_zero (by norm_num : 0 < I.im)) (exp_ne_zero _)) h.symm


lemma condition_four : ‖(π : ℂ) * (I / 2)‖ < thetaLatticeMinNorm I := by
  calc ‖(π : ℂ) * (I / 2)‖ = Real.pi / 2 := by
         simp [div_eq_mul_inv, Real.norm_of_nonneg Real.pi_pos.le]
       _ < Real.pi := by linarith [Real.pi_pos]
       _ ≤ _ := radius_ge

lemma condition_three : ‖(π : ℂ) * ((1 + I) / 2)‖ < thetaLatticeMinNorm I := by
  have hn : ‖((1 + I) / 2 : ℂ)‖ < 1 := by
    have h := Complex.sq_norm ((1 + I) / 2 : ℂ)
    norm_num [normSq_apply, div_re, div_im] at h
    rw [norm_div, Complex.norm_ofNat]
    nlinarith [norm_nonneg (1 + I : ℂ)]
  calc ‖(π : ℂ) * ((1 + I) / 2)‖ = Real.pi * ‖((1 + I) / 2 : ℂ)‖ := by
         rw [norm_mul, Complex.norm_real, Real.norm_of_nonneg Real.pi_pos.le]
       _ < Real.pi := by nlinarith [Real.pi_pos]
       _ ≤ _ := radius_ge

lemma theta_four_zero : DLMF.Elliptic.jacobiThetaFourTau ((π : ℂ) * (I / 2)) I = 0 := by
  have h := DLMF.JacobiElliptic.je22a_thetaFour_add_half_tau 0 I
  simp only [zero_add, DLMF.JacobiElliptic.je22a_thetaOne_zero, mul_zero] at h
  simpa [mul_div_assoc] using h

lemma theta_three_zero : DLMF.Elliptic.jacobiThetaThreeTau ((π : ℂ) * ((1 + I) / 2)) I = 0 := by
  have h := DLMF.JacobiElliptic.je22a_thetaThree_add_half_pi ((π : ℂ) * (I / 2)) I
  rw [theta_four_zero] at h
  convert h using 1 <;> congr 1 <;> ring

lemma counterexample_four : ¬ (∃ S : ℂ,
    HasSum (fun j : ℕ => thetaGamma (2 * (j + 1)) I * (I / 2) ^ (2 * (j + 1)) /
      (2 * (j + 1))) S ∧
    DLMF.Elliptic.jacobiThetaFourTau ((π : ℂ) * (I / 2)) I =
      jacobiThetaFourNullTau I * cexp (-S)) := by
  rintro ⟨S, _, h⟩
  rw [theta_four_zero] at h
  exact (mul_ne_zero (DLMF.JacobiElliptic.je22a_thetaFour_zero_ne_zero (by norm_num : 0 < I.im)) (exp_ne_zero _)) h.symm

lemma counterexample_three : ¬ (∃ S : ℂ,
    HasSum (fun j : ℕ => thetaBeta (2 * (j + 1)) I * ((1 + I) / 2) ^ (2 * (j + 1)) /
      (2 * (j + 1))) S ∧
    DLMF.Elliptic.jacobiThetaThreeTau ((π : ℂ) * ((1 + I) / 2)) I =
      jacobiThetaThreeNullTau I * cexp (-S)) := by
  rintro ⟨S, _, h⟩
  rw [theta_three_zero] at h
  exact (mul_ne_zero (DLMF.JacobiElliptic.je22a_thetaThree_zero_ne_zero (by norm_num : 0 < I.im)) (exp_ne_zero _)) h.symm

#print axioms condition
#print axioms counterexample
#print axioms condition_three
#print axioms condition_four
#print axioms counterexample_three
#print axioms counterexample_four
end DLMF.Theta

newIssues.name: DLMF.EllipticIntegrals.symEllIntRC_sq_eq
newIssues.status: Analytical branch counterexample; not formalized in Lean; statement retained
newIssues.detail: At x=-I,y=1 the hypotheses permit the point. The left RC(-1,1) integral has strictly negative imaginary part, whereas the transformed RC(-I/2,(1-I)/2) integrand has strictly positive imaginary part. Both converge, including the integrable left square-root singularity at t=1. The strict-half-plane variant is already proved as symEllIntRC_sq.

newIssues.name: DLMF.EllipticIntegrals.symEllIntR_half_hasSum_mean
newIssues.status: Lean counterexample, using only standard axioms; original statement retained
newIssues.detail: For n=2,a=1 take z0=(-3200-798*i)/169 and z1=(-1120+3102*i)/169. Their mean A=(-2160+1152*i)/169 lies in the slit plane and the normalized deviations have norm 65/72<1. Original and normalized principal square roots give opposite signs in the asserted homogeneity. The current assumptions do not prevent this branch mismatch.
newIssues.reproductionSource:
import DLMF.EllipticIntegrals.SymmetricSpecialCases
import DLMF.EllipticIntegrals.SymmetricQuadratic
open Complex Set
open scoped Real
namespace DLMF.EllipticIntegrals
noncomputable def branchNodes : Fin 2 → ℂ := ![((7-57*I)/13)^2, ((33+47*I)/13)^2]
noncomputable def branchMean : ℂ := (1/(2:ℂ))*∑ i, branchNodes i
lemma branchMean_eq : branchMean = (-2160+1152*I)/169 := by
  norm_num [branchMean, branchNodes, Fin.sum_univ_two, Complex.ext_iff,
    Complex.div_re, Complex.div_im, Complex.mul_re, Complex.mul_im, pow_two]
lemma branchMean_ne : branchMean ≠ 0 := by
  rw [branchMean_eq]; norm_num [Complex.ext_iff, Complex.div_re, Complex.div_im]
lemma branchNorm_eq : (fun i => branchNodes i / branchMean) =
    ![((13+5*I)/12)^2, ((13-5*I)/12)^2] := by
  rw [branchMean_eq]; ext i; fin_cases i <;>
    norm_num [branchNodes, Complex.ext_iff, pow_two, Complex.div_re, Complex.div_im,
      Complex.mul_re, Complex.mul_im, Complex.normSq]
lemma branch_domain : branchNodes ∈ Carlson.carlsonRSlitDomain := by
  intro i; fin_cases i <;> apply ei19c_sq_mem_slitPlane <;>
    norm_num [branchNodes, Complex.div_re]
lemma branchMean_slit : branchMean ∈ slitPlane := by
  apply mem_slitPlane_iff.mpr (Or.inr ?_)
  rw [branchMean_eq]
  norm_num [Complex.div_im]
lemma branchNorm_close (i : Fin 2) : ‖1-branchNodes i / branchMean‖ < 1 := by
  have he := congrFun branchNorm_eq i
  rw [he]; fin_cases i <;>
    norm_num [Complex.ext_iff, pow_two, Complex.norm_def, Complex.normSq, Complex.div_re,
      Complex.div_im, Complex.mul_re, Complex.mul_im, Real.sqrt_div]
lemma testMean_counterexample : symEllIntR 1 (fun _ : Fin 2 => 1/2) branchNodes ≠
    branchMean⁻¹ * symEllIntR 1 (fun _ : Fin 2 => 1/2)
      (fun i => branchNodes i / branchMean) := by
  have hR {u v : ℂ} (hu : 0<u.re) (hv : 0<v.re) :
      symEllIntR 1 (fun _ : Fin 2 => 1/2) ![u^2,v^2] = u⁻¹*v⁻¹ := by
    have hc : (∑ _ : Fin 2, (1/2:ℂ)) = 1 := by norm_num
    have h := symEllIntR_sum (fun _ : Fin 2 => (1/2:ℂ))
      (ei19c_slit2 (ei19c_sq_mem_slitPlane hu) (ei19c_sq_mem_slitPlane hv))
      (by rw [hc, Gamma_one]; norm_num)
    rw [hc] at h
    rw [h]
    simp only [Fin.prod_univ_two, Matrix.cons_val_zero, Matrix.cons_val_one,
      cpow_neg, show (1/2:ℂ) = 2⁻¹ by norm_num, sq_cpow_two_inv hu, sq_cpow_two_inv hv]
  rw [branchNorm_eq]
  change symEllIntR 1 (fun _ : Fin 2 => 1/2) ![((7-57*I)/13)^2, ((33+47*I)/13)^2] ≠ _
  rw [hR (by norm_num [Complex.div_re]) (by norm_num [Complex.div_re]),
    hR (by norm_num [Complex.div_re]) (by norm_num [Complex.div_re]), branchMean_eq]
  norm_num [Complex.ext_iff, Complex.div_re, Complex.div_im, Complex.mul_re, Complex.mul_im,
    Complex.inv_re, Complex.inv_im, Complex.normSq]
#print axioms testMean_counterexample
end DLMF.EllipticIntegrals

lemma testMean_hasSum_false : ¬ HasSum
    (fun N => branchMean ^ (-(1:ℂ)) * ((ascPochhammer ℂ N).eval 1 /
      (ascPochhammer ℂ N).eval ((2:ℂ)/2) *
        symEllIntT N (fun _ : Fin 2 => 1/2) (fun j => 1-branchNodes j / branchMean)))
    (symEllIntR 1 (fun _ : Fin 2 => 1/2) branchNodes) := by
  intro H
  have h := (symEllIntR_hasSum_T 1 (fun _ : Fin 2 => (1/2:ℂ))
    (fun j => branchNodes j / branchMean) (by norm_num [Fin.sum_univ_two])
    branchNorm_close).mul_left (branchMean ^ (-(1:ℂ)))
  have hs : (∑ _ : Fin 2, (1/2:ℂ)) = (2:ℂ)/2 := by norm_num
  rw [hs] at h
  have he := H.unique h
  apply testMean_counterexample
  simpa only [cpow_neg_one] using he
#print axioms testMean_hasSum_false
end DLMF.EllipticIntegrals

nextHornPDEWork:
Next target: hornG2_G3_second_order_pde in Appell/DefinitionsAndSeries.

The new generic recurrence/PDE framework already matches all Horn equations.
For G2, the x recurrence parameters are kappa=-1, alpha=0, beta=-1,
rho=-1, upper a and b', gamma=1-b. For y, swap a/a' and b/b'.
The coefficient identity is
 (m+1)*(b+n-m-1)*C(m+1,n)=(a+m)*(b'+m-n)*C(m,n).

For G3, x parameters are kappa=-2, alpha=beta=-1/2, rho=-4,
upper a'/2 and (a'+1)/2, gamma=1-a. For y swap a and a'.
The coefficient identity is
 (m+1)*(a+2*n-m-1)*C(m+1,n)
   =(a'+2*m-n)*(a'+2*m-n+1)*C(m,n).
After multiplying the generic expanded PDE by x, its lower Euler polynomial
is the negative of thetaX(a+2*thetaY-thetaX); rho=-4 supplies the corresponding
negative quadratic numerator. Likewise G2 with rho=-1.

All Gamma shift arguments are nonintegral under the original hypotheses;
Gamma_add_one proves these recurrences without any new exceptional cases.
The existing ghaR4_regular_of_nonint supplies Gamma nonvanishing.

Normal convergence on a local polydisc can come from existing summability,
without extracting the old private coefficient bounds. Pick positive real A>|x|,
B>|y| strictly inside the available region and apply hornG2_summable or
hornG3_summable at the complex points A,B. Taking Summable.norm and rewriting
norm_mul/norm_pow gives Summable(norm(C(m,n))*A^m*B^n).
For G3, delta=(1/4-|x|-|y|)/4 and A=|x|+delta,B=|y|+delta work.
For G2 one can use A=(|x|+1)/2,B=(|y|+1)/2 since the target lies inside
|x|+|y|<1/4 while G2 summability holds throughout the unit bidisc.

Remaining calculus bridge: expand the Theta products into ordinary partials.
ThetaXThetaX F = x*Fx + x^2*Fxx; ThetaXThetaY F = x*y*Fxy.
Reverse mixed partials agree using the new mixed-series formula and index swap.
One-variable holomorphy of the series follows from existing
Complex.differentiableOn_tsum_of_locally_dominated on a smaller coordinate disc;
this gives the differentiability needed for the product rule in Theta squares.
No numerical approximation or sector asymptotics is required.
